top.title: HALO Wins Court Order Blocking Merck's Keytruda SC in Europe
top.summary: A Dutch patent court ruled that Merck's Keytruda subcutaneous formulation infringes Halozyme's MDASE patent, ordering Merck to cease manufacturing and sales across eight European markets. The ruling does not affect Keytruda's intravenous version. This marks another legal victory for Halozyme against Merck, though the company clarified that its separate ENHANZE technology and licensing business remain unaffected.

top.title: Bayer Seeks Kerendia Label Expansion in Non-Diabetic CKD
top.summary: Bayer announced FDA acceptance of a supplemental new drug application for Kerendia (finerenone) to treat chronic kidney disease in non-diabetic patients. The approval is based on positive phase III FIND-CKD trial data showing the drug significantly delayed kidney disease progression and reduced cardiovascular-kidney events. This expansion broadens Kerendia's addressable market and strengthens Bayer's cardiovascular and renal portfolio, with the drug already approved for diabetic CKD and heart failure in multiple markets.

top.title: Roche Gets FDA Approval for Another Label Expansion of Tecentriq
top.summary: Roche received FDA approval for Tecentriq in combination with chemotherapy for adjuvant treatment of stage III deficient DNA mismatch repair (dMMR) colon cancer. The phase III ATOMIC study demonstrated a 50% reduction in recurrence or death risk, with 86% disease-free survival at 36 months versus 76% for chemotherapy alone. top.title: NVS Wins FDA Nod for Label Expansion of Immunology Drug Rhapsido
